slice: NORTH-WEST outer districts — Gò Vấp, District 12 (Quận 12), Tân Phú, Hóc Môn. Kept SEPARATE from the other SIGHTS_HCMC*.json files.

sights.address: Islet in the Vàm Thuật River, ferry from end of Trần Bá Giao St, Ward 5, Gò Vấp, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A ~300-year-old 'floating temple' on a 2,500 m² islet in the middle of the Vàm Thuật River, reached only by a short ferry (~10k VND). More than 100 colourful ceramic-mosaic dragons cover the roofs and columns of the Buddhist-Taoist shrine, a city-recognised architectural-artistic heritage site since 2010. One of Gò Vấp's few genuine landmarks.

sights.address: 1460 Phan Văn Hớn, Xuân Thới Thượng Commune, Hóc Môn, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: A 73,000 m² national historical monument (ranked 2002) on the site where French colonial authorities executed revolutionary leaders after the failed 1940 Nam Kỳ (Southern) Uprising. A memorial temple, exhibition house and monuments sit among bamboo, lotus ponds and areca palms — the anchor heritage site of rural Hóc Môn.

sights.n: Bà Điểm & the Eighteen Betel Garden Villages (18 Thôn Vườn Trầu)
sights.address: Bà Điểm Commune, Hóc Môn, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: The historic areca-and-betel-growing belt around Bà Điểm, famed since the 18th century and a cradle of the 1940 Southern Uprising — the Southern Party Committee sheltered in its gardens. Today a living cultural-heritage landscape of remnant trầu (betel) gardens and revolutionary memory rather than a ticketed attraction.

sights.address: 30 Bờ Bao Tân Thắng, Sơn Kỳ Ward, Tân Phú, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
sights.w: AEON's first shopping mall in Vietnam, opened 11 Jan 2014 — a ~70,000 m² Japanese-anchored complex in the Celadon City estate that made Vietnam the third country (after Malaysia and China) with a large-scale AEON MALL. A CGV cinema, food court, indoor playground and 200+ brands make it the western suburbs' main weekend gathering place.
